{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABgL-rrw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhJpCwY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 160, "title": "Remove implicit pause on tab visibility changes and keep playback state user-controlled", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator currently treats changing to another tab or hiding the page as an **implicit user pause**. This is unexpected: the user did not press Pause, the shared playback button changes from Pause to Play, and returning to the tab requires an extra action to resume.

The maintainer's decision is **explicit playback control only**: do not automatically pause *or* automatically resume due to document visibility. Keep the ordinary Play/Pause button for deliberate user actions. Cleanly remove the obsolete auto-pause behavior, including tests and documentation; **no compatibility shims, config flags, dormant paths, or scaffolding for possibly reintroducing the feature later**.

Current `main` at `a8c7f5fc3710615c1d6517c99cdcacd12a49be71`:
- [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) registers `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.hidden) { clearInput(); if (playing) pause(); } })`. The `pause()` call changes `playing`, updates the UI, flushes audio, and saves SRAM.
- `start()` blocks when `document.hidden`, so a cartridge selected while the page later becomes hidden may fail to enter the playing state.
- `animate()` already bounds elapsed-time catch-up and per-callback frames, but background tabs may throttle/suspend `requestAnimationFrame`.
- [`web/tests/display.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/tests/display.spec.js) explicitly asserts the current hidden-tab auto-pause behavior; [`web/tests/demo-launch.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/tests/demo-launch.spec.js) tests loading while hidden and waiting for a separate Play click. The [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md) states "A hidden tab pauses."

## Intended behavior

**The app's Play/Pause state changes only because of a deliberate playback action or a genuine lifecycle/error condition—not because a browser tab became hidden/visible.**

| State before switching tabs | While tab is hidden | After returning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Playing | Remains logically **Playing** (browser may throttle/suspend execution) | Continues playing without another Play click |
| Manually Paused | Remains **Paused** | Remains paused until user presses Play |

- Hiding/showing the page must **not** call `pause()`, `start()`, `togglePlayback()` or modify `playing` simply because visibility changed.
- The Play/Pause button and playback status must continue reflecting the same user-selected state. Do **not** label hidden-tab throttling as a user-requested Pause.
- Releasing held keys/touch inputs when focus or visibility is lost is still appropriate to avoid stuck SNES buttons. Keep that cleanup, decoupled from playback state, ideally reusing existing `clearInput()` / blur handling rather than duplicating lifecycle flags.
- Returning to a visible page must not simulate elapsed background time by fast-forwarding many frames. Preserve or simplify the existing bounded-frame timing mechanism so the animation resumes naturally from the last emulated state. Audio scheduling must not accumulate a long backlog or burst/stutter; preserve sound-user-gesture restrictions and the ability to recover if browser audio is suspended.
- Recognize browser reality: a hidden tab may suspend or throttle `requestAnimationFrame` and audio. **Continuous 60fps execution or uninterrupted sound in the background is not required or promised.** The requirement is that the emulator does not turn that browser behavior into a persistent, user-visible Pause state.
- Selecting a cartridge while loading asynchronously and becoming hidden must not introduce an artificial requirement to click Play on return. Keep explicit user-gesture/autoplay rules, ROM validation, save restoration and protection; when a valid user-initiated load completes, its intended playing state remains consistent even if actual frame callbacks are throttled while hidden.
- Keep `pagehide` SRAM persistence and normal save protections. Do not regress save-on-explicit-pause, reset, cartridge replacement, per-ROM SRAM identity, or recovery from storage errors.
- Normal errors can still halt gameplay for correctness; do not remove those guards in an effort to prevent visibility-induced pause.

## Clean implementation requirement (important)

This is an intentional **behavior change**, not a compatibility exercise. Implement the simplest correct model rather than preserving the old one:
- Remove the hidden-tab auto-pause code and any now-unnecessary `document.hidden` playback gating, redundant state/mode tracking, obsolete comments and compatibility helpers.
- Replace tests that encode "hidden means paused" with tests of the new invariants. **Do not keep an old test or fallback path solely to support the removed auto-pause feature**.
- Do not add an "auto-pause enabled" setting, session/localStorage flag, legacy migration, delayed implicit pause, future-proof switch, or another button to compensate.
- Avoid unrelated refactors or changes to Rust/Wasm emulation, CRT/Pixel display, game ROMs, public assets, audio/volume UI or touch layout. Keep the code small and straightforward.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] With a genuine running Wasm game, dispatch/trigger hidden and visible transitions: `#play` stays **Pause**, status stays **Playing**, and no hidden-tab call reaches `pause()` or changes `playing`. After visibility returns, emulator frames/input progress without another Play gesture.
- [ ] When a game was **manually paused**, switching away and back preserves the paused state and frame buffer; no automatic resume occurs.
- [ ] Held keyboard/touch controls are cleared appropriately on blur/visibility loss; no stuck keys on return. Test gamepad/keyboard/touch behavior after returning, without altering user-selected playing/paused state.
- [ ] Verify timebase reset/bounded catch-up after a simulated long background interval: no huge frame burst or audio backlog; no WebGL/CRT presentation glitch or unhandled error.
- [ ] Cover a user-selected bundled/local ROM whose asynchronous load finishes while hidden: valid load/restore leads to the intended playing state without another click when visible; preserve blocked/failed save restoration and invalid ROM safety.
- [ ] Update `display.spec.js`, `demo-launch.spec.js` and any other tests affected by previous auto-pause assumptions; verify actual new behavior rather than weakening/removing assertions. Update README/help copy to remove "A hidden tab pauses".
- [ ] Preserve explicit Play/Pause and Reset-to-playing, volume/mute, CRT/Pixel selection, cartridge switching, full twelve-button mobile controls, audio permission handling, save lifecycle and GitHub Pages artifact/subpath behavior.
- [ ] Run the applicable production build and full relevant browser integration suite, plus repository CI checks required for the changed files. Report actual results and any optional checks omitted; do not imply unrun tests passed.

## Optional validation

Check real Chrome, Firefox and mobile Safari tab switching, tab suspension, screen locking and browser audio policies. These are optional external-device checks, not a reason to leave old auto-pause compatibility code.

## Post-merge verification

After merge, verify the new `main` GitHub Pages deployment and test the actual public app: switch away while playing, return, and confirm playback is not left in Pause; repeat with explicit manual Pause. Record actual run/URL/results. This is **post-merge-only**; open a separate `task` Issue for any confirmed publication regression when invoked, without background monitoring.

## Related work

- [Issue #122](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/122): unified cartridge insertion and autoplay.
- [Issue #128](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/128): reset continues playing.
- [Issue #142](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/142): CRT display and continuity.
- [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable.
